en.title: Main religions
en.summary: The religions practised in English-speaking countries and the legal idea of freedom of religion.

paragraphs: Religion shapes holidays, buildings, law and daily habits. This lesson describes the religious landscape of Britain and the United States and shows how to talk about proportions and groups.

Christianity has been the main religion in Britain for about fifteen hundred years, but the number of people who say they have no religion has grown, and there are also large communities of Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs, Jews and Buddhists. In England, the Church of England is the established church, with the monarch as its supreme governor. In the United States the First Amendment keeps church and state separate. A class discusses religion in Britain.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Christianity is the largest religion in Britain.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Yes. There are Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs, Jews and Buddhists, and many people have no religion.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: In England, the Church of England is the established church. Scotland has the Church of Scotland, which is independent of the state.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: There is no official church. The constitution protects the freedom to practise any religion.

paragraphs: **1. There is and there are for existence.** The verb agrees with the noun that follows. See Introduction to Grammar: Present tense, being and having.

blocks.html:
FormExample
there areThere are Muslims and Hindus.
there isThere is an established church.
there has beenThere has been a decline.
there are noThere are no official religions.

paragraphs: **2. Superlatives and proportions.** Use the largest, the oldest, and expressions such as the majority of and a minority of. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives.

blocks.html:
Adjective or phraseExample
the largestthe largest religion
the oldestthe oldest church
the majority ofthe majority of people
a minority ofa minority of the population

items: Secular means not religious; atheist means a person who does not believe in a god.
A place of worship can be a church, mosque, temple, gurdwara or synagogue.
The established church is the church linked officially to the state.
Freedom of religion means everyone can choose their religion.

paragraphs: Religious freedom is protected by law in all English-speaking democracies. Schools usually teach about the world's religions without preferring any one of them.
